Structured
Programming
Part 2: Visualizing Algorithms
with Flowcharts
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
•
Explain how flowcharts represent algorithms
visually.
•
Identify the common symbols used in
programming flowcharts.
•
Represent sequence, selection, and iteration
using flowcharts.

Flowcharts
A flowchart is a diagram that
uses symbols and arrows to
represent the steps and
decisions in an algorithm.
Flowcharts allow programmers
to plan and understand the
logic of a program before
writing code.
Arrows connect the symbols
and show the order in which
the steps occur.
Different symbols have
different meanings.

START/END
The START/END symbol indicates
where a process begins or ends.
Every flowchart should have at
least one start symbol and one
end symbol.

Process
The Process symbol represents
an action or operation being
performed.
Most statements in a program
are represented using process
symbols.

Arrow
Arrows show the direction that
control flows through the
process.
They connect flowchart symbols
and indicate what step happens
next.

Input/Output
The Input/Output symbol
represents data entering or
leaving a program.
Common examples include
receiving user input or displaying
output to the screen.

Decision
The Decision symbol represents a
condition that can evaluate to
either true or false.
Depending on the result, the flow
follows a different path.

Subprocess
The Subprocess symbol
represents a task that has been
defined elsewhere, such as a
function.
It allows complex processes to be
broken into smaller, reusable
parts.

Visualizing Control
Structures
Flowcharts can be used to visualize the
three fundamental control structures used
in programming: sequence, selection, and
iteration.

Visualizing Sequence
A sequence is represented by a series of process symbols connected by
arrows.

Visualizing Selection
Selection structures use decision symbols to show different paths that may
be taken based on a condition.

Visualizing Iteration
Iteration
structures use
arrows that
loop back to
an earlier
point in the
flowchart,
representing
code that
repeats until a
condition is
met.
